title: Surrounded Regions
pattern: Flood-fill from the border, then flip the rest
statement: Given a board of `X` and `O`, **capture** every region of `O`s that is completely surrounded by `X` (on all four sides) by flipping those `O`s to `X`. A region that touches the border of the board can not be captured. Modify the board in place.

example.why: The three O's in the middle are enclosed and get flipped. The O in the bottom row touches the border, so it survives.

picture: Picture each region of `O`s as a puddle on the board. A puddle that touches the edge can drain away, so it is safe; a puddle with no way to the edge gets filled in with `X`. So first walk inward from every `O` on the edge and mark its whole safe puddle with `E`. Then sweep the board: every `O` still unmarked is surrounded and becomes `X`, and every `E` turns back into `O`.
idea: Deciding directly whether a region is surrounded is awkward. The opposite is easy: an `O` is **safe** exactly when it is connected to an `O` on the border.
So start a flood-fill from every border `O` and mark everything it reaches with a temporary letter `E` (*escaped*).
Afterwards every `O` that is still an `O` was never reached from the border — flip it to `X`. Turn the `E` marks back into `O`.

say.7: A helper that marks a whole safe region: it turns this `O`, and every `O` connected to it, into `E`.
say.8: Is this cell outside the board, or anything other than an `O`?
say.15: Then there is nothing to mark here.
say.17: Mark the cell `E`: it is connected to the edge, so it will not be captured.
say.20: Mark onward through the cell below (the helper calls itself).
say.22: And through the cell to the right.
say.23: And through the cell to the left.
say.26: Step 1: check the left and right edges, row by row.
say.27: Is there an `O` on the left edge?
say.28: Then mark its whole region as safe.
say.29: Is there an `O` on the right edge?
say.30: Then mark its whole region as safe.
say.32: Then check the top and bottom edges, column by column.
say.33: Is there an `O` on the top edge?
say.34: Then mark its whole region as safe.
say.35: Is there an `O` on the bottom edge?
say.36: Then mark its whole region as safe.
say.39: Step 2: sweep the whole board, row by row…
say.41: An `O` that was never marked cannot reach the edge: it is surrounded.
say.42: So capture it: turn it into `X`.
